subject: crowbar
label: crowbar, in the place of the game's models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_shotgun.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_sqknest.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, D where the asset was D, B, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief's outline is a crowbar: a straight shaft with a hooked claw at one end. In sides.png the asset is a flat plate, tapering to a point in the LEFT, RIGHT and FRONT views and with no hook in any view. Its outline is a flat sliver, not a crowbar's.

M2.reason: Measured length is 32.3 against the brief's 32, within 1%. The brief gives no width or height, so only the length is held to it.

M3.reason: The brief asks for a hooked claw, a round steel shaft and a grip end. The asset has none of these: no claw in any view (sides.png, first-person.png, in-hand.png), and the 6-triangle slab is one plate with no separate parts. The claw is missing, so M3 is at most 1 and I score it 0 because the shape itself is wrong.

M4.reason: The brief asks for red paint over steel, worn to bare metal at the tips. The asset is grey throughout (sides.png, first-person.png), with no red anywhere. The grey is clearly off from the brief's red.

M5.reason: The brief's wear to bare metal at the tips is barely there: only faint lighter edges at the ends in sides.png (TOP, BELOW) and no worn pattern. Stripes, paint wear and the red finish the brief implies are absent.

M6.reason: Measured by the line-up test, as the rubric directs: the asset was picked 0 of 3 times as the non-Valve model (the judges chose C, C, D where it was at D, B, C), so it passes. Capped at 2 here.

M7.reason: A crowbar's front is its claw end, and the asset has no claw to read as a front. In the FRONT and BACK views it is a thin diamond, and it lies on its origin as a flat plate rather than as a held weapon.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks return no errors. It has 6 triangles, far below any bound for a weapon. The views show a closed solid: no open face, no inside out and no floating part a player can see.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the game's crowbar sits at the upper right, held as a hooked bar, while the asset floats at the upper left with no hand around it. In attack.png the slab leaves the picture in frames 1, 4 and 7 to 9, and no grip is visible to show it is held.
